slides.headline: She trained in Kerala and Bangalore before building a career in Australian child psychiatry. In 2026, the King honoured her for it.
Professor Valsamma Eapen was named an Officer of the Order of Australia in the 2026 King's Birthday Honours
slides.body: The Governor-General's official list, issued June 8, 2026, recognized her work in psychiatry, child and adolescent mental health, neurodevelopmental research and tertiary education - one of ten Indian-origin Australians honoured that year.

slides.headline: Born in Kerala, she trained at India's National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences before moving to the UK, then Australia.
slides.body: She now holds the chair of infant, child and adolescent psychiatry at UNSW Sydney, where her research into neurodevelopmental conditions like Tourette Syndrome and autism has produced a quality-of-life scale adopted by teams in 32 countries.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when its medical graduates end up shaping psychiatric care standards used across dozens of countries.
slides.body: Eapen's path from Kerala's medical colleges to an Officer of the Order of Australia shows Indian psychiatric training compounding into research that's now used far beyond either country.
